$comment: Sources support two modes — the indexer does not care which you use:
The example below uses MODE B because the two source CSVs already live in R2,
while their original local copies may only exist on your previous laptop.
1. Run `bun run verify:r2:remote` and copy the EXACT object keys from its
report into `path` values. Do not guess the key names.
2. Run `profile` and confirm the canonical mapping (fix `columns` if needed).
3. Run a `--sample 100000` pass before the full job.
4. Never paste R2 keys in here: they are read from the environment only.
MODE B needs R2_ACCOUNT_ID / R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY exported
in your own terminal session (Object Read on company-intel-data is enough),
because Wrangler's login cannot be handed to a local Bun/Node process.
Switching to MODE A instead: copy the objects down with
and point `path` at the local files.
$commentRawCacheDir: MODE B only: each R2 object is streamed to this directory once (via a .part
file that is renamed only after the byte count matches R2), so a re-run resumes
from disk instead of downloading 60 GB again. Budget ~1.0x the input size here
in addition to workDir, or set it to null to stream without caching.
$commentObjectSizes: Companies per object and contacts per object are fixed in code (SHARDING in
src/shared/search/index-format.ts) because the Worker derives the object key for
a document reference from those same constants. Changing them requires a new
index format version and a rebuild.
